svg.title: A load is prepared, touching nothing the world shows, then committed, or abandoned
svg.desc: Prepare reads the whole scene record: it refuses a record still linking prefabs, reads every page's component names and column shapes, checks the plan for entities recorded twice, rows not listed, a component twice in a page and two pages of one domain, reserves an entity id per saved entity without bringing it to life, stages every value field by field with references bound, and reads the hierarchy from Parent, refusing a cycle. Any failure gives the reserved ids back and returns the reason with the report; the world is unchanged. Commit registers what the file declares, keeps each saved identity unless another entity holds it, places every row in its final page and builds Children, and returns the entities and the report. A load prepared for another world adds nothing; one prepared before the world's components changed is prepared again.

g.text: Names and shapes
A record that still links prefabs is refused: links are expanded first. Then page by page,
each column's length is checked against the page's rows, and each component's name is
resolved: current, formerly, retired, not saved, declared by the file — or unknown,
which refuses the load.
The plan, checked
With every name known, the record's plan is checked as a whole: an entity recorded
twice, a row whose entity the record does not list, a component twice in one page, two
pages of one domain for one entity. Any of them refuses the load.
Ids reserved
One entity id per saved entity, reserved: held for this load, not alive, handed to no
one else. No query, no system, no other load can see or take them.
Values staged
Every value is read field by field, by name, into a staged row; every reference to an
entity is bound to the id reserved for it, or to nowhere when the file does not hold it.
Each adaptation becomes an entry of the report.
Hierarchy read
The tree is read from each entity's Parent; a cycle refuses the load. The result is a
Prepared load: everything checked, nothing shown.
A prepare needs no World: off the frame, it reads the world's catalogue instead.
Commit
What the file declares and the world lacks is registered. Each saved identity is kept,
unless another entity already holds it. Every row lands in its final page at once, and
Children is built beside each Parent. The result: the entities, and the report.
Commit returns no error. Prepared for another world, it adds nothing (NotLoaded);
prepared before the world's components changed, it is prepared again first.
Or nothing at all
A failure anywhere in prepare gives the reserved ids back and returns the reason, with
the report of what had been read. A prepared load can also be abandoned on purpose.
Either every entity of the file arrives, or the world is exactly as it was.
